Jack_Benny_09_15_1953: The Jack Benny Show from September 15 1953

rv: Who cares that this is a syndication print with different theme music, This episode features...Marilyn Monroe! Yep, She guest stars on this episode, and even sings a song! No wonder this show was a hit! With such talented guest stars as this, it's not surprising this show is among the longest running sitcoms of all time.

Yes, that is definitely Marilyn Monroe. Great fun show too - so many of these Jack Benny shows are still so fresh and funny after all these years. I remember Jack Benny being one of my very favorite shows as a small child in the late 50s - early 60s, and I can still see why!

The surprise for me in watching this programme was the voice of Paul Frees as the narrator. Were this his radio show, he would have used Don Wilson or a supporting cast member. This television show is set up very differently than his radio show of the same era. Benny opened with a monologue, which he mainly did in his earliest radio days. By 1953, his radio opens consisted of the cast gathered around or Jack already into the premise of his show with a cast member trading dialogue. rv: This is actually good comedy. "That Lum, you can't trust him anymore. He'll believe anything you tell him." Abner has a classic case of addictive behavior; Lum the co-dependent is intent on fixing him. Next to Vic and Sade, Lum and Abner were the best comedy team on old time radio--too bad they never quite made it in video format. Despite the really bad kinescope quality of this clip, I enjoyed watching it.
